name: Punctured-Triangle Corner-Cap Obstructions
statement: Let $X=\{a,b,c,x\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z$ with $Z\ne\varnothing$. Delete the punctured triangle $\mathcal L_\triangle$, $\{a,x\}$, and every $\{a,c,x\}\cup S$ for $S\subseteq Z$. The complement is a learning space rooted at $\{a,b,c,x\}$. Its endpoint repair sets are $\{a,b,c,x\}$ and $Z$, so its empty-endpoint pendant extension is a contraction-minimal nonlearning partial cube of order $2^d-2^{|Z|}-6$.
proof: Translation by $\{a,b,c,x\}$ splits the missing family into two anchor-hereditary blocks and one local state, proving union closure; a complete deletion argument proves accessibility. Explicit union and intersection witnesses determine the endpoint holes. Their repair sets cover all coordinates, so the critical-antipodal pendant criterion applies; the three disjoint deleted blocks give the order.
